cues: The angel takes no part in his own show.
His only supernatural virtue seems to be patience.
Hens peck at him, invalids tear out his feathers, even kind people throw stones to make him stand.
He refuses mothballs, which the neighbour says angels eat, and lives on eggplant mush.
Once, when he lies so still they think he is dead, they burn his side with a branding iron.
He wakes in tears, shouting in his unknown language, and beats his wings in a storm of dust.
After that they are careful: his calm was not that of a hero at rest, but of a cataclysm in repose.
